## Caller contract
`withAuth`-wrapped routes in `pages/api/accounting/bank/*` (+ `bank-match-confirm.ts`); migrations `327_*` (VAT subtype), `514/515/519/520/526`, `*bank_*`. Every DB function takes `companyId` first. VLM services are stateless; the caller persists under its own `companyId`.

## Main function signatures
- `lockBankTransactionForUpdate(companyId, txId)` — company-scoped `FOR UPDATE`; `null` for missing/other tenant; THROWS outside a request transaction (an implicit one locks nothing); 5s `lock_timeout` → `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` (test with `isBankTransactionLockTimeout`, structural), restored to `DEFAULT` on the SUCCESS path — `SET LOCAL` lasts to the end of the TRANSACTION, and both confirm arms and `voidPaymentDocument` call this FIRST, so without the restore the 5s budget governs every lock they take afterwards (pinned both ways — present on success, ABSENT after a 55P03, because in a `finally` it would raise 25P02 over the typed error — in `tests/unit/services/bankAllocationRowLock.test.ts`).
- `allocateTransaction(companyId, txId, …, opts?)` / `splitAllocateTransaction` — post the JE; VAT account via `systemAccountResolver` (subtype) then codes 1140/2120. Its two pre-write refusals (missing row, status ≠ `imported`) throw `BankAllocationRefusal` — `isBankAllocationRefusal`.
- `reverseReconciledTransaction(companyId, txId, userId, opts?: {postingAgent?, reversalDate?})` — unwind, contra, reset to `imported`, ALL in one savepoint. Contra date = original entry's when that period is open, else today. Refuses PRE-WRITE on a closed/locked period; `no_period` is not refused (`createJournalEntry` auto-creates the year). Omit `postingAgent` and the contra stays `human:<userId>`.
- `validateBankSupplierPayment` / `planSupplierAllocationLines` / `planSupplierPaymentApplication` (in `ap/`) throw `SupplierPaymentRefusal` for a refusal and NOTHING ELSE — catch that, re-throw the rest, or a dropped connection reaches the browser as a 400. `planSupplierPaymentApplication` was the exception until 2026-09-10: it threw bare `Error`s, and `supplier-allocations.ts` therefore had to catch EVERYTHING and answer 400 with `err.message` — schema and column names in front of the user, on a status `withAuth` COMMITs, monitored as their mistake. Typing the four throws is what let that catch be narrowed, so the two changes only make sense together.
- `findBankTransactionsByReferences(companyId, refs[], acct?)` — ONE query (join on `unnest($refs)`, two arms, one per column), `Map` by trimmed reference, 25 candidates per reference, each carrying `matchedReference`+`matchedColumn`. Returns every candidate; the caller decides what >1 means. `findBankTransactionAllocationStates(companyId, ids[])` — `{id,status,matchedJournalLineId}` for a whole set in one query; it reads BOTH columns deliberately — a row carrying `matched_journal_line_id` is in the ledger whatever `status` says, and **a fixture that sets only the status passes while production fails**. `getBankTransactionStatus` stays for one-line tools, and exists so an MCP refusal can be answered from a READ: both write services write BEFORE they can fail, and a refusal frees the idempotency key, so the retry writes a second time.
- **Bulk/batch path**: `contactDirectoryService.suppliersBelongToCompany(companyId, ids[])` / `customersBelongToCompany` — ONE query per set, empty set skipped; the bulk allocate loop depends on them, and checking a counterparty per line is 500 round trips. `partitionAllocationLines` (`allocationApplyRoute`) is what REFUSES on that path, pre-write, splitting the lines into postable and skipped — `invoiceSkipReason` beside it is exported and called by nothing.
- `importBankStatement` / `importParsedTransactions(…, {skipAutoPost, skipPostImportEffects})`, `importStatementForAgent`, `undoImportBatch` (null for another company; deletes only `imported` rows, reports the rest), `startReconciliation`/`completeReconciliation`/`createAdjustmentEntry`, `applyRules` (priority ASC = highest), `listAgentPostings` (`reversed` from `reversed_at`, never `status`), `buildExpenseJournalFromReceipt` (pure), `extractWithVlm`/`extractBankStatementWithVlm`/`extractStatutoryDocWithVlm`.
- `tableLockUnavailable()` (`bankTxLock`) — `LOCK TABLE bank_transactions IN ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE NOWAIT` under its OWN savepoint. `true` = a DDL-mode lock is held on the TABLE. `matchTransaction` asks it before reading a `55P03` as "line claimed", because the match UPDATE runs under `withBankLockBudget`'s 5s `lock_timeout`, which bounds every wait THAT statement takes and so fires on an index build too (the row lock restores the default after itself, so nothing else in the request inherits the budget); refused → `BankMatchUnavailableError` ("retry in a moment"), counted as `skippedUnavailable`, never `skippedRaced`. It cannot be consulted from `lockBankTransactionForUpdate` itself — that SELECT is outside a savepoint, so its 55P03 aborts the tx and the probe answers 25P02 (K-140).
- `rulePattern(rule)` (`bankRulesSuggestionPass`) — the ONE place a rule row becomes an ILIKE pattern, for BOTH arms. `match_type` is nullable and NULL means `exact`; `String(rule.match_type)` reads `'null'` and widens it to `contains`.
- `getAutoPostSettings`/`updateAutoPostSettings`/`autoPostRunSnapshot`/`sweep` (`autoPostGateService`), `undoRun(companyId, runId, userId)` (`autoPostUndoService` — one savepoint per row; a contended/failed/reconciled row is skipped and counted per reason (`skippedBy`), and the run is marked undone ONLY when `skipped` is 0 (`undone` in the result). A provisional JE already reversed by hand is finished without a second reversal (`alreadyUndone`); a row still `allocated`/`matched` with nothing linked is a `failed` skip, never already-undone. Throws the contention — `bank-auto-post` 503 + Retry-After for a held row (D11; 409 only for a retryable STATE conflict) — only when no row was written at all; otherwise 200 with the counts. Each row is locked and re-read first; a row a later journal may already correct is an `offsetByHand` skip, described in `handOffsets` (line and journal: date, amount, description), and nothing is posted for it). Two recorded decisions (`bank-auto-post` `confirmHandCorrection` / `undoAnyway`, both `audit_log`, both close the run when no row is left tagged): `markCorrectedByHand` posts nothing and is accepted only for a person-made journal that, with the posting, nets every non-bank account of it to zero (within a cent); `undoAnyway` declares the journal unrelated and undoes the line. Refusals are `HandCorrectionRefusedError` (400, pre-write).

## Business rules
- **A bank account is a `gl_accounts` row with `account_subtype='bank'`** — `bank_transactions.bank_account_id` FKs to `gl_accounts(id)`; the name misleads. The `bank_accounts` table is vestigial (0 rows prod); only `bank_feed_connections` may point at it. Use `hasBankAccount`/`countBankAccounts`, never a count of `bank_accounts`.
- Status flow `imported → matched → allocated → reconciled`; allocation is atomic under `withTransaction` (JE + status).
- **Direction follows the SIGN of the line, on every arm.** `isSpent = amount < 0` decides DR/CR for supplier and customer allocations too — a refund booked as a payment moves the bank by TWICE the line (R261,651.64 found on Velocity). The VAT KEY follows the alloc TYPE, not the direction (a refund reverses INPUT tax). The 4-way match runs only when `isSpent`; a `customer_payments` row is minted only when `!isSpent`. Every settler asks `signMismatchReason` (`bankLineDirection`) — it refuses a ZERO line outright, because the downstream throw it fronts would land mid-write.
- **A VAT code on a supplier/customer allocation posts NO VAT** (control-account settlement): one predicate, `gl/settlementVat.isControlAccountSettlement`, read by `allocateTransaction` and by `gl/ruleVatResolution` for the sweep. `allocateTransaction` ANDs it with `Boolean(entityId)` (an entity-less call falls through to the account arm); the rule path picks on `allocType` alone. `gl/bankContraVat` drops the code on a `bank`-subtype contra — pass that flag as `undefined` when the account is absent from the map, never `?? false`.
- **Attended paths never coerce a VAT choice; `autoPostRuleLine` (unattended) does** and returns `vatDenied` (from the account's `vat_input_denied` flag, tallied into `autoPostVatDenied`); the unattended line builder is `buildAutoCreateLines` (`bankRulesMatchingHelpers`), which is where the `netAmount` defect lived. `auto_create_entry=false` rules are suggestion-only. BOTH directions are pinned by `tests/unit/services/bankVatDisplayAgreesWithJournalDb.test.ts` (real Postgres) — it is the only gate on this rule, so don't delete it when a mock would be quicker.
- **A settlement must write its payment DOCUMENT and its ALLOCATION row** — `supplier_payments` + `payment_allocations` on the AP side, `customer_payments` + `customer_payment_allocations` on the AR side. Those are the only tables `bankAllocationUnwind` reads, so a bare `amount_paid` write is irreversible — and, computed in JS, a lost update too. Both arms of `bank-match-confirm` obey this: `confirmSupplierMatch` → `applyBankLineToSupplierInvoices`, `confirmCustomerMatch` → `confirmReceiptMatch`. Never assign `supplier_invoices.balance` (GENERATED since mig 201 → 428C9). **An over-payment is REFUSED, not capped, on both arms**: `apAgingService` and `debtorsManagerService` read the invoice tables alone, so the excess would part the control account from the aging invisibly. A caller that HANDS IN allocations (the MCP apply tool) may leave a remainder; a screen deriving them may not.
- **`withAuth` COMMITs below 500**, so every refusal must be decided from READS before the first write; past the first write the only safe answer is 500. Exception, and it must be shown: a refusal raised before any write may keep a 4xx (`bank-match-confirm` answers a contended line 503 + Retry-After, D11; it was 409).
- **Every pg error aborts the transaction**, not just 40P01/40001/25P02 — so a swallowed failure needs a SAVEPOINT, not a code whitelist (`bankTransferAutoLink`, the import auto-post sweep). If the savepoint's own ROLLBACK fails, rethrow: nothing saves that case. Give each savepoint a unique name; a duplicate SHADOWS rather than errors.
- **Row locks**: LOCKED — `allocateTransaction`, `splitAllocateTransaction`, `reverseReconciledTransaction`, `matchTransaction`, `unmatchTransaction`, `excludeTransaction`, each auto-post candidate. NOT locked, deliberately — read-only paths, the post-UPDATE re-read, `deleteTransactions` (its `status='imported'` predicate is the guard) and `bulkAcceptTransactions` (it knowingly relabels allocated rows). `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` is re-issued EVERY call, never memoised: it is subtransaction-aware and `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` restores `0`. Bulk loops sort by transaction id — a total lock order turns a deadlock into a wait. A raced/locked row is SKIPPED and counted (`skippedRaced`, `autoPostSkippedLocked`, `autoPostTruncatedRules`; `MAX_RULE_CANDIDATES`=500), never allowed to abort the run, and every counter reaches the UI.
- **CANONICAL LOCK ORDER — every path takes these rows in this sequence, always**: (0) `bank_reconciliations` — the session row (D12): FOR SHARE by every line writer (the session a line is stamped with, taken INSIDE `lockBankTransactionForUpdate` / `lockBankTransactionsInIdOrder` before the line, or the one `matchTransaction` / `autoMatchTransactions` names), FOR UPDATE only by complete, cancel and reopen (an adjustment posts a journal, so it SHARES — D12 round 2), never after holding one of its lines and never share→update on a session another request can see. The order holds PER LINE, not per request: a multi-line writer (bulk allocate, the sweeps) posts line N's journal and then shares line N+1's session. That cannot close a cycle only because the three exclusive holders wait on no journal and on no line outside their session — keep it so (brk-d12 B1 measured the 40P01 when the adjustment held it exclusively); (1) `bank_transactions`, (2) `customer_payments`/`supplier_payments`, (3) `customer_invoices`/`supplier_invoices` (a SET of them `ORDER BY id`), (4) `gl_journal_entries`/`gl_journal_lines`. Two paths taking any pair in opposite orders deadlock: Postgres kills a victim with **40P01**, which `withAuth` answers as a 500 — the money path reporting a server fault to a user whose only mistake was arriving at the same instant as somebody else.

  **Build this table MECHANICALLY, never by reasoning about which pairs can run together.** An `UPDATE` and a `DELETE` take a row lock exactly as `FOR UPDATE` does, so enumerating only the explicit `FOR UPDATE`s is what hid three inversions across rounds 7–9 — `voidSupplierPayment` was missing from this very table while it deadlocked. The enumeration walks every function that touches more than one of these relations (`FOR UPDATE`, `LOCK TABLE`, the `lock*ForUpdate` helpers, `fetch{Invoice,Bill}Candidates`, and every `UPDATE`/`DELETE`), records the ORDERED sequence, and derives the cycles from that LIST. inversions, and they do not look like locks. The round-9 enumeration walked every `sql` template in
`src/`, `pages/` and `scripts/`, tagged each by relation family (BANK / PAY / INV / GL), and kept
every file touching more than one — 14 files, of which four were missing from this table and three

  `archiveExecutionService` (which deleted from all four relation families) was removed on 2026-10-05.
No path deletes posted history any more, so the NO ACTION FKs into those relations (38 at K-071, 40
measured 2026-10-05 on migration 852) are no longer a lock-order or FK-order question for this table.

  **The one exemption, and it is structural rather than an unreachability argument**: a row INSERTed by this transaction cannot be locked by any other transaction, because no other transaction can see it. So `createJournalEntry` + `postJournalEntry` on a brand-new entry does not put `gl_journal_entries` into a path's ordering; a `FOR UPDATE` or reversal of a PRE-EXISTING entry does. That is the difference between `confirmCustomerPayment` (exempt) and `cancelCustomerPayment` (not). The one wait a NEW entry does impose is on its generated NUMBER — see the journal INSERT row in the table (migration 857): it is a real lock, taken in the INSERT's BEFORE trigger and held to commit, not an exemption.
  Five paths take a lock they would not otherwise need, purely to fix the order, and REMOVING ANY RE-OPENS THE DEADLOCK: both `confirm*Match` arms call `lockBankTransactionForUpdate` before reading the document they settle; `voidPaymentDocument` resolves its bank line from an UNLOCKED peek so it can lock the LINE before the payment; and `confirmCustomerPayment` / `processSupplierPayment` / `cancelCustomerPayment` / `voidSupplierPayment` call `lock{Customer,Supplier}PaymentForUpdate` as their FIRST act. Multi-invoice loops go `ORDER BY invoice_id` for the same reason the candidate fetchers do. Pinned by `tests/unit/services/bank/confirm{Customer,Supplier}Match.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/{paymentVoidService,supplierPaymentVoid,supplierPaymentWorkflowService}.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/ar/customerPaymentLockOrder.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/bank/bankAllocationUnwind.test.ts`, and — measured on real SQL — `tests/integration/k071-lock-order-deadlock.int.test.ts` and `k071-void-lock-order.int.test.ts` (whose readiness probes filter `pg_stat_activity` by their own `application_name`: the statement text alone matches any session in the cluster, and this fixture database is shared, so an unscoped probe returns early and the test passes on the defect). The bank-before-journal pair in `capture/evidenceAttachmentService` and `POST /api/accounting/provisional/[jeId]/attach` is pinned by `tests/unit/services/capture/evidenceAttachmentService.test.ts` and `provisionalAttachRouteLockOrder.test.ts`, both asserting the ORDER off `sqlMock.mock.calls` — until round 10 the only test there DOCUMENTED THE OLD ORDER in its docblock, which is an instruction to put the deadlock back.
  Contention is ANSWERED, never faulted: `core/lockContention.isLockContention` classifies BOTH `55P03` (our `lock_timeout`) and `40P01`, and every settlement lock maps them to its own retryable typed refusal — `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` (409), `PaymentLockTimeoutError`, and — from `fetch{Invoice,Bill}Candidates` — a `ReceiptRefusal`/`SupplierPaymentRefusal` carrying **`retryable: true`** ("retry in a moment"). That FLAG is what makes contention answerable: those two classes also carry every refusal about the BOOKS, so without it the confirm arms could not tell "this bill is cancelled" from "a peer holds it" and answered both `apiResponse.badRequest` — the same instant of contention answering 409 when the peer held the bank LINE and 400 when it held the invoice, 400 being the status this codebase reserves for the user's own mistake and monitors as such. `confirm{Supplier,Customer}Match` return `kind:'contended'` for a retryable refusal and `bank-match-confirm` answers it `apiResponse.conflict`; every one of them is decided pre-write, so the 4xx `withAuth` COMMITs commits nothing. **NINE routes answer this event 409, TWO absorb it as a counted skip, THREE swallow it in-service (R-065)** — the r15 census is a CHECKER-RESOLVED reverse call graph from the five construction sites, and `docs/audits/remediation/K-071/fix.md` lists every entry file it reaches and how each answers. Round 11 said four and was counting DIRECT importers of `plan{Receipt,SupplierPayment}Application` / `validateBank{ReceiptApplication,SupplierPayment}`; the four it found — `bank-match-confirm`, `ar/receipt-match/confirm`, `customer-allocations`, `supplier-allocations` — classify contention themselves. The other four reach the same event THROUGH an intermediary and so name none of those symbols: `allocateTransaction` calls `recordSupplierBankPayment` / `autoApplyCustomerReceipt`, which call the plan functions, and the three lock helpers raise it one row earlier. Those are `bank-transactions-action` (nine verbs), `bank-transactions-manual`, `supplier-payments-action` and `customer-payments-action` — blanket-catch routes that answered 400 (the manual one, 500) until r13 gave them `core/retryableContention.isRetryableContention`, the UNION of the four predicates, tested before the blanket branch. Measured, not argued: a probe rejecting `allocateTransaction` with `BankTransactionLockTimeoutError` answered 400 on `bank-transactions-action` while `k071-lock-order-deadlock.int.test.ts:195` pinned the identical event at 409. Any new caller of the plan/validate functions, DIRECT OR TRANSITIVE, joins that list: test the retryable flag BEFORE the plain refusal, or contention falls through to the 400 branch. **A census of the files that import a symbol is not a census of the routes that can raise it** — walk the call graph through intermediaries. Round 14 walked ONE hop from `autoPostRuleLine` and missed `applyRules` (`bank-rules-action` apply, `bank-rules` POST) and `undoRun` (`bank-auto-post` undo): the rule sweep now skips-and-counts the whole union (`autoPostSkippedLocked`, both routes 200), and `undoRun` skips-and-counts it too, answering 409 only when nothing was written (K-071 r19). **STILL OPEN (R-065):** `autoPostGateService.sweep` catches every per-row failure with no savepoint, so a contended `allocateTransaction` aborts the request transaction and the next statement is a 25P02 — `smart-categorize` directly; `bank-transactions-bulk-commit` and `bank-feeds/[id]/extension-ingest` through `importParsedTransactions`, whose own savepoint then discards the whole sweep as "non-fatal". **STILL OPEN (R-060):** those four routes catch EVERYTHING and answer a 4xx. For contention that is safe ONLY because on those four every member either aborts the request transaction (55P03/40P01 on the outer tx: `withAuth`'s COMMIT degrades to a rollback) or is confined to a savepoint with nothing written before it. **The union is NOT pre-write as a property of its own**: a member surfacing through a savepoint that rolled back CLEANLY leaves the request transaction live, and whatever the request wrote earlier COMMITs behind the 4xx — measured r14 on `applyRules`, 400 with line A committed. A new caller must establish which shape it has before answering 409 (`core/retryableContention.ts`). For any NON-aborting throw raised after `allocateTransaction` has posted its journal or `voidSupplierPayment` has reversed one, the catch commits a partial write behind a failure response. Pre-existing, and a plan/apply split rather than a status fix. Mapping 40P01 is the second line of defence, not a licence to stop ordering locks.
  **Do not settle a suspected cycle by argument.** "No cycle is reachable" was written into this file in round 8 about `voidSupplierPayment` and was wrong — round 9 measured `40P01 deadlock detected` on the fixture with that order restored, the void itself the victim, the route answering 400. Prove it by outcome (two interleaved pool clients) or fix the order.
- match/unmatch/exclude refuse `allocated AND matched_journal_line_id IS NOT NULL` (`BankTransactionAllocatedError` → 400). `reconciled` is deliberately excluded (its journal pre-dates the link) — EXCEPT a line IN a completed reconciliation (D12, below); `allocated` with a NULL line is half-finished and allowed through. Undoing a posted allocation is `reverseReconciledTransaction`'s job.
- **A COMPLETED reconciliation is immutable (D12, Hein 2026-10-04).** A line is IN session S when `reconciliation_id = S` and status `reconciled`/`matched`; the same id on an imported/allocated/provisional/excluded line is a STALE stamp (start re-claims it) and its writes proceed. Any write that would add, remove or change a line of a completed S is refused BEFORE its first write with `ReconciliationCompletedError` (`RECONCILIATION_COMPLETED`, "… is completed — reopen it first"): match/unmatch/exclude on a line in it (`lockForStatusWrite`, the shared `reconciledCash` rule), match or auto_match INTO it (the session locked FOR SHARE first; auto-match's candidate reads also require `in_progress`), every reversal/void through `refuseLockedCash` kind `completed` (and `provisionalSettlementVoid`), complete/cancel (header FOR UPDATE first, status read under it) and adjustment (header FOR SHARE — it posts a journal). ONE answer: 409 via `@/lib/apiReconciliationCompleted` — in `respondToUnhandledError`, the blanket-catch routes and `bankMatchRefusalStatus` — and an MCP refusal (REFUSAL_CODES); `ReconciledCashError`'s other kinds keep 400. Reopen is the only way back. A write that turns a STALE-stamped line `matched` outside a session (match without a session, bulk accept, both evidence attaches) clears a stamp whose session is not in progress in the same UPDATE (`openStampOnly`, FOR SHARE, so an unlocked writer waits for a completion in flight); an in-progress stamp is kept. NOT guarded, by design: `archiveExecutionService` step 6 (register). **Annotations are out of scope**: notes, cc/bu, `suggested_*`, `allocation_batch_id`, `auto_post_run_id` and the asset/fleet LINK ids (`linked_asset_id`, `linked_fleet_fuel_id`, `linked_fleet_service_id`, mig 853) may still change on a completed line; the asset/fleet link routes never change status, journal line or stamp (`bankAssetLinkService`). Round 2 (brk-d12): allocate, split, both bank-match-confirm settlement arms and `undoAnyway` raise the 409 before their own status refusal (`reconciledCash.refuseLineOfCompletedReconciliation`); `delete` / `bulk_accept` refuse the WHOLE request when any named line is in a completed session (`refuseLinesInCompletedSession`); a generic journal reversal refuses the cash of a completed session (`refuseJournalCashOfCompletedReconciliation`, `completed` kind only); the `openStampOnly` writer that locks no line first (bulk accept) runs under `underStampBudget` (5 s → 503); a completed session's `matched_count` is its `reconciled` lines. `autoPostUndoService.undoRun` counts a chain line in a completed session as `failed`, as it did the old `ReconciledCashError`.
- **Dedup is a CONTENT HASH of (date, amount, description, balance)** — no reference in it, so two genuinely separate same-day identical rows collapse (known). Do NOT add the reference: pre-2026-09-07 rows carry none and would stop matching their own statement. Known: the 2026-08-27 `parseAmount` comma fix MOVED the hash, so re-importing an SA-formatted CSV lands the corrected row beside the wrong one — undo the batch first.
- **The statement reference lives in `reference`; `bank_reference` holds a FEED'S EXTERNAL ID** (0 prod rows). So `reference` wins outright and `bank_reference` is consulted only for a reference that matched nothing. Match EXACTLY after `btrim(x, E' \t\n\r\f')` — never LIKE (`INV-1` would take `INV-10`), never bare `btrim` (strips spaces only), never `\v` (pg reads `E'\v'` as the letter). Mig 519's expression indexes must stay character-for-character identical to the query or the planner reverts to a company scan — `bankTxRefCandidateQuery` is exported UNRUN so the DB-gated test can `EXPLAIN` the service's REAL statement; the previous test planned a pasted copy and stayed green through a regression. Don't drop the column: `customer_payments` and the feed dedup key read it.
- `addBankTxAttachment`: magic-byte check → ownership read → INSERT, and **keep that order** — the attachments table has no `company_id` of its own. `listImportBatches` counts `transactionsRemaining`/`transactionsAllocated` LIVE from `bank_transactions.import_batch_id`: `bank_import_batches.transaction_count` is what the import wrote and an undo leaves it unchanged. `listAgentPostings` returns `reversalOfId` beside `reversed`.
- Open-banking Basiq/Tink/Plaid are NOT implemented (they used to INSERT invented rows, K-018): `createBankFeedConnection` refuses them, `syncBankFeed` throws `BankFeedProviderNotImplementedError`, and routes must map it to a 4xx or `withAuth` discards the `markSyncFailed` audit trail.
- **A session claims allocated lines as their own match** (`bankReconciliationClaim`, 2026-09-30). Start claims, for this company + bank account, `feed_state='posted'`, `transaction_date <= statement_date`: every `imported` line (auto-match works on these) and every `allocated` line whose `matched_journal_line_id` is a line of THIS bank account on a POSTED, unreversed (`reversed_at IS NULL`) journal dated `<= statement_date` — counted matched at once (confidence 1.0). Never `reconciled`/`excluded`; never a line stamped by an IN-PROGRESS session; a COMPLETED session's stale stamp is re-claimed. `matched_count`/`unmatched_count` and completion use the same predicate (`countsAsMatched`), so completion reconciles `matched` + self-matched lines. Completion recomputes the live GL balance first (`updateReconciledBalance`, which never touches a completed session). Auto-match inside a session reads only its own/unclaimed imported lines `<= statement_date` against GL lines `<= statement_date`.
- `autoMatch` is not atomic (per-row); its `matched_journal_line_id NOT IN (…)` subquery IS company-scoped — unscoped, another tenant hid journal lines from this one. `completeReconciliation` requires a zero difference AND ≥1 matched transaction, reported as `completed:false` (a success, never a refusal — `start`/`autoMatch` have already written). Cancelling releases `matched` rows to `imported` and merely detaches `allocated`/`provisional`/`excluded`; it re-asserts `status='in_progress'` in the DELETE. Cancel's `dry_run` runs every guard and writes nothing, and a POSTED adjustment journal blocks the cancel — found through `gl_journal_entries.source_record_id`. Adjustments use mig 526's own column, NOT `source_document_id` (FK'd to `captured_documents` since mig 409).
- Coverage/cash: `cash.balance.v1` (ledger) is `cashBalanceService`, `cash.statement.v1` (sum of `bank_transactions.amount`) is a different question — never net them. The OTHER services answering the statement question are `bankAccountStatusService.balance` and `kpiDashboardService`; add a fifth cash answer in neither. `kpiChartsService` is the mirror of the LEFT-JOIN-ON-vs-WHERE rule below and drifts with it. `bt.amount = jl.debit - jl.credit` on all 9,097 matched prod rows, so `glOnlyMovement - statementOnlyMovement` is an EXACT identity; a non-zero `unexplainedResidual` means a `bank_opening_balance` with no journal behind it. Neither service filters `is_active` (a deactivated account still holds cash — `deactivatedWithBalance` REPORTS them, it does not exclude them); `getCashBalance` spans subtype `bank` AND `cash`; the posted/date restriction belongs in the LEFT JOIN's ON + a CASE, never a WHERE (that deletes draft-only accounts).
- `getCashBalance(companyId, asOf, { exclusive: true })` answers the OPENING balance — the closing balance of the day BEFORE `asOf`. An option, not a day the caller subtracts: JS date arithmetic on this UTC+2 server is what put 291 journals in the wrong period. `cashFlowDirectService.fetchOpeningCash` delegates here rather than keeping its own copy.
- Display columns come from the POSTED JOURNAL, never a cached label: `ALLOCATED_ACCOUNT_LATERAL` (with `AND bl.gl_account_id = bt.bank_account_id` — load-bearing, or the sibling of a user-picked line reads as the destination) and `POSTED_VAT_LATERAL` (`'standard'` asserted from the presence of a VAT-account line, NULL over zero lines). Mig 520's `allocation_rule_{id,name}` carry the rule; `allocated_entity_name` is ALWAYS the account. `allocation_batch_id` is CLEARED by allocate/split/reverse, or a batch reverse would unwind a posting it never made (mig 514/515). `recordAllocationBatchLines` THROWS unless every id was stamped — a posted journal outside the reversible set is the failure the batch id exists to prevent; `getAllocationBatchLines` LEFT-joins (returning `transactionExists`) and returns `null` for another tenant's batch so the caller renders the generic NOT_FOUND.
- Dates: build journal dates with `fmtDate` from `@/lib/neon`, never `toISOString()` — pg returns `transaction_date` at LOCAL midnight and UTC rendering dates a 00:30 SAST line to the previous day (wrong month at a period boundary). `getBankTransactions` pages on an opaque keyset cursor whose predicate must stay in lockstep with an ORDER BY ending `bt.id DESC`; a malformed cursor, a non-calendar date, a non-UUID id, or a cursor combined with a non-zero `offset` all throw `InvalidCursorError` before any query.
- Parsers: ABSA is mapped by HEADER NAME (both the current and legacy layouts) and reads SA-style "1 234,56"; `YYYYMMDD` is checked before the separator split and validated with `isRealCalendarDate`. QIF strips header LINES, not whole blocks (`!Type:Bank` shares a block with transaction #1). The Reference column is matched against exact header names and left UNSET when blank. Not every format carries one: `bankCsvParserStandard` (standard_bank/capitec/nedbank), the ABSA legacy layout and every PDF parser have none.
- VLM env: `VLLM_BASE_URL`, `VLM_MODEL`, `VLLM_API_KEY`, `VLLM_TIMEOUT`; `isVlmAvailable()` for health.

## Feed lifecycle (bank sync v1)
- **Feed lifecycle (migration 675).** `bank_transactions.feed_state` is `pending | posted | removed`, independent of `status`. Manual and statement rows are `posted`. A non-posted row is visible in the review queue and nowhere else: every accounting mutation refuses it, and every statement total, coverage figure and KPI filters `feed_state = 'posted'`.
- **Three layers, all required.** (1) Locked mutators call `assertFeedPosted` from the row they hold, before the first write (`bankFeedStateGuard.ts`). (2) Set-based writers carry `feed_state = 'posted'` in their candidate predicate. (3) Trigger `trg_bank_tx_feed_state_guard` refuses any accounting-column change on a non-posted row and any source-field change on a processed feed row (SQLSTATE 23514, `BANK_TX_FEED_GUARD:`). A new writer that forgets (1) or (2) gets a 500 from (3); the trigger is a backstop, not the user-facing refusal.
- **Legal lifecycle moves:** `pending -> posted` and `pending -> removed` only.
- **Reader census ratchet.** `tests/unit/guards/bankFeedStateReaderCensus.test.ts` classifies every file whose SQL reads `bank_transactions` (filtered / exempt: reason). A new reader file must be classified; the ratchet is per file, so a new statement in an already-classified file still needs a posted predicate by hand.
- **`bank_transactions_posted` view (migration 675) is `SELECT *`**, which freezes its column list to `bank_transactions`' shape at creation time. Any later migration that drops or retypes a `bank_transactions` column must DROP and recreate `bank_transactions_posted` — a bare `ALTER TABLE` does not propagate through a `SELECT *` view.

- 2026-09-18 (L1 r3): **a bulk batch mixing an invoice-named line with a FIFO line for the SAME contact is order-dependent.** The batch posts sorted by transaction id (deadlock avoidance), so if the FIFO line sorts first it consumes the bill the named line was going to pay, that line is then refused for exceeding the outstanding, and the whole batch rolls back — all-or-nothing, loudly, nothing mis-posted. `dry_run` simulates in the SAME posting order (previously in payload order, which made a three-line batch's preview disagree with itself), but it does not predict this refusal: the invoice-named pre-check in `bulkAllocationSkip` measures against the balance before any FIFO line spends it. Send invoice-named lines in their own batch, or `auto_apply: "none"` on the others.
- 2026-09-18 (L1 r3): **`bankAllocationService.ts` is 837 lines, over the 300-line cap**, and this programme grew it. Not refactored here deliberately — it is the file every bank write goes through, and splitting it in the same change as a money-behaviour change would make both unreviewable. The natural seams, if someone takes it on: the VAT resolution block at the top (`resolveVatAccountId`, the fallback codes), `splitAllocateTransaction`, and `reverseReconciledTransaction` — each is self-contained and none is called by the other two.
- 2026-09-18 (L1 r2): the bulk `dry_run` preview reads the open documents WITHOUT `FOR UPDATE` and states what it cannot know in `preview_caveats` — a line whose date falls in no fiscal period posts its payment or receipt and applies none of it, which no preview can see because the journal does not exist yet.
- 2026-09-18 (L1): `allocateTransaction`'s `opts.autoApply` is a MODE (`'fifo' | 'none'`), not a boolean, and it returns `application` — what the line settled and what is left `onAccount` — for every supplier/customer line that named no document. Default `'fifo'`. `bankRuleAutoPostLine` reads the rule's own `auto_apply` column (migration 676, on `bank_categorisation_rules`: `bank_rules` holds no rows and no posting path reads it). An unreadable value on a rule is the DEFAULT, not `'none'` — a rule row written before the column existed must not reproduce the state this change ends.
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r6): the hand-reversed (`alreadyUndone`) branch of `undoRow` calls `unwindBankAllocationApplication(companyId, jeId)` on both shapes before finishing the line — a hand reversal touches only the ledger, so the supplier payment / customer receipt the posting minted and the bill / invoice it settled still read as paid; the clean undo unwinds them through `reverseReconciledTransaction`, and the finished line now ends in the same subledger state (payment cancelled, document reopened, 0 allocations).
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r5): `undoRow` is ONE path for the matched and provisional shapes — resolve the posting journal, check its reversal state, THEN scan for a blocker. The matched shape (what `bankRuleAutoPostLine` writes) used to scan first, so a hand-reversed posting with a later reclass on its account told the user to reverse a legitimate journal; it is `alreadyUndone` on both shapes now (the matched line gets the same reset `reverseReconciledTransaction` makes). Census reason for `auto_post_run_id`: trigger 675 refuses tagging a non-posted row on UPDATE, but its CHECK omits the column on INSERT — no writer does that; registered.
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r4): the undo-anyway projection is REAL balances (`autoPostUndoProjection`: net of every posted line on each touched account, minus the posting's effect after) — a posting-plus-one-journal sum hid one overstatement per dialog on a split correction. The scan bound is POSTING TIME only; the `entry_date` bound was not what bought the speed and it let a backdated (month-end) reclass through. `autoPostHandOffset` / `autoPostHandCorrection` are classified in `bankFeedStateReaderCensus` as exempt: their `bank_transactions` reads are keyed on `provisional_je_id` / `matched_journal_line_id` / `auto_post_run_id`, which a non-posted feed row cannot carry (trigger 675).
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r3): a blocking journal that does NOT net the posting out (a reclass, a partial correction) gets "reverse that journal first, then undo" — once reversed through the product the chain walk sees it off the books and the undo nets to zero; "mark as corrected" is offered only when it nets out; "undo anyway" shows each account now and after the undo (`autoPostUndoProjection`) before anyone confirms. Undo-anyway refuses (400, declaration rolled back) any outcome that is not an undo — a line reconciled meanwhile, a re-reversed posting. The scan was bounded by entry_date here; r4 dropped that (see below). Per-journal line checks compare `company_id::TEXT` so stale statistics cannot pick the company-wide index (8,000 earlier or later journals: ≤ 88 ms stale or analyzed).
- 2026-09-11 (R-079 r2): detection FAILS CLOSED — any later person-made journal (source not `auto_*`, `posting_agent` human/legacy or NULL) that moves a NON-bank account of the posting back blocks the undo, so a reclass (the common hand correction) is caught; the bank leg alone never blocks. "Mark as corrected" is decided by the NET (posting + journal = 0 on every non-bank account), so a later receipt can no longer close a live posting; "Not the correction — undo anyway" is the second recorded choice. The scan is one statement per row bounded by the posting's non-bank accounts: 8,000 later bank journals cost 5–25 ms (was 2,874 ms). Known: a person-made credit to an expense account after a posting blocks every earlier auto-posting on it until the user decides.
- 2026-09-11 (R-079): `undoRun` no longer reverses a posting a person already offset with a MANUAL journal (no `reversal_of_id`, no `reversed_at` — the undo applied the correction twice, E1 ending −60 with the run read undone). Decided by ledger evidence, never by an equal amount alone: a later posted non-reversal journal still on the books that moves the posting's accounts back AND is either linked (source record = the bank line, or the posting's source document) or person-made, owned by no other bank line, and wholly within the posting (only its accounts, opposite direction, ≤ the posted amount). Such a row is skipped `offsetByHand`; the user reverses their journal or confirms it via `markCorrectedByHand`. Known limit: a reclass to an account the posting never touched is indistinguishable from an unrelated one and does not stop the undo. `docs/audits/remediation/R-079/fix.md`.

This closes the direct-save bypass: inactive, foreign, missing or wrong-slot assignments are refused before the write, while allocation itself continues through the same shared policy when it creates its journal.

Also open: `invoiceSkipReason` (`allocationApplyRoute`) is exported and called by nothing — left in place, since wiring it up is a behaviour change; and `vlmBankMatchService` has no callers.
- 2026-09-09: **`bulkAcceptTransactions` over-reported success for rows it never touched.** It read `.count` off an UPDATE with no `RETURNING` — always undefined — and fell back to `ids.length`, so the operator was told every id they sent had been accepted, including rows the `status IN ('imported','allocated')` predicate skipped. `deleteTransactions` twenty lines above already carried both the `RETURNING id` and the comment explaining why; this is the instance that comment did not cover. Now `RETURNING id` + `result.length`. Worse than the K-111 defect it neighbours: that one under-reported to zero, this one reported success that had not happened.
